items.stem: At a conceptual level, what problem does the Model Context Protocol aim to solve?

options.text: Providing a common way for AI applications to connect to tools and data sources

options.text: Training large language models from scratch

MCP is not a UI framework.

items.stem: Which TWO are core MCP primitives a server can expose? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: tools are callable capabilities a server exposes.
Correct: resources are data a server exposes to clients.
A firewall is a network control, not an MCP primitive.
A spreadsheet is not an MCP primitive.

items.stem: When designing an MCP server for an internal service, a sound security principle is to:

options.text: Expose only the capabilities needed, with authorization (least privilege)
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits what a connected client can do.

options.text: Expose every internal operation for flexibility
Skip input validation to simplify the server
options.rationale: Input validation is essential for safe exposure.

options.text: Share one admin credential with all clients
options.rationale: Shared broad credentials violate least privilege.

items.explanation: Correct: least privilege limits what a connected client can do.
